subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: Should memory-core implement checkpoint/resume as a validated resumable shadow generation, direct incremental writes to the live DB, or defer resumable full reindexing for now?
rationale: Source inspection proves the reliability gap, but durable generation identity, incomplete-index visibility, orphan cleanup policy, and any public memorySearch configuration are product/API choices rather than a strict mechanical fix.

options.title: Resumable shadow generation
options.body: Persist generation/checkpoint state for a compatible shadow DB and publish only after validation, preserving the known-good-index invariant while allowing restart resume.

options.title: Direct incremental live writes
options.body: Write checkpointed progress into the live DB with explicit incomplete-generation filtering and status semantics, accepting a larger migration and config surface.

options.title: Defer resume support
options.body: Keep atomic full rebuild behavior and rely on cache reuse, retry, and orphan cleanup until maintainers prioritize a broader memory indexing redesign.

recommendation.title: Resumable shadow generation
recommendation.body: Persist generation/checkpoint state for a compatible shadow DB and publish only after validation, preserving the known-good-index invariant while allowing restart resume.

likelyOwner.reason: The earlier reindex lineage and prior keep-open review route the product-shape decision most directly to steipete, with vincentkoc as a likely implementation owner.
